taxonomy.note: Accepted species; South American native and introduced in Texas.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Verbena brasiliensis and gives its native range in South America; Texas is explicitly listed as introduced.
TexasInvasives.org identifies Brazilian vervain as introduced to the U.S., reports it throughout central/east/north Texas, and describes it as a significant invasive species.
NPSOT classifies Verbena brasiliensis as an invasive plant and notes its threat of displacing native plants.
The project source pool contains seven user observations marked wild, supporting strong local encounter value but not native status.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Native status remains FAIL regardless of local abundance. Invasive comparison retention is a separate learner decision and is excluded from native totals.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the architecture: a tall plant with long bare internodes and an open candelabra-like panicle made of many short compact flower spikes; the leaves are simple, narrow, sharply serrate, and not lobed.
diagnostic_traits: introduced South American annual or short-lived perennial, often 0.9–2.3 m tall
erect strongly 4-sided green stems with long internodes
opposite simple elliptic to oblanceolate leaves, sharply serrate above midblade
leaves sessile/subsessile and not deeply lobed
open panicle with several orders of opposite branching
many short compact terminal spikelets rather than a few long spikes
tiny violet-purple flowers and prolific small mericarps/seeds

confusers.separator: V. scabra has broad harsh sandpaper leaves and very long slender spikes; Brazilian vervain has narrow simple serrate leaves and many short compact spikes in an open panicle.
V. xutha has deeply 3-lobed leaves and coarse hispid/glandular foliage; Brazilian vervain leaves are simple and unlobed.
A separate introduced ornamental/naturalized Verbena with dense rounded flower heads on long peduncles; do not collapse it into V. brasiliensis.

learner_role.reason: Regional invasive source plus seven user wild observations make Brazilian vervain highly relevant for crew identification. Requires explicit batch/comparison approval before installation.

installation_guardrail: Native status remains FAIL. Install only if Calvin explicitly approves retention as a labeled invasive/non-native comparison; exclude from native totals.
